description: Shared Renovate policy for millsymills-com and millsmillsymills. Extend it from a repo with {"extends": ["local>millsymills-com/.github:renovate-config"]} inside the org, or {"extends": ["github>millsymills-com/.github:renovate-config"]} from the user account.
Rationale, measurements, and the automerge boundary are in millsymills-com/millsymills-com-org docs/adr/0007-renovate-over-dependabot.md. Change the policy here, not per repo.

Delete a repo's .github/dependabot.yml when you onboard it. Two bots on one manifest means duplicate PRs and races on the same lockfile. Dependabot *alerts* stay on -- they are declared in tofu and Renovate reads them.

pre-commit.description: The pre-commit manager is disabled by default and must be opted into, or the pre-commit packageRule below never matches anything.

description: Advisory-driven updates skip both the cooldown and the Monday window, because for a known-exploitable version the delay is the risk. They do not skip the human: the 7-day cooldown exists because a freshly published version is when a compromised release is most likely to still be live, so waiving it and the reviewer at once would drop both defenses in the same step.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Monthly `uv lock --upgrade` (and the equivalent for other managers) to refresh transitive pins that no manifest edit would touch. Dependabot has no equivalent; this is the gap that motivated the switch.

packageRules.description: Majors are never automerged. A grouped merge carried docker/metadata-action v5 to v6 with nobody reading the changelog (resurgent#160); majors get their own PR and a deliberate look.
Never bump the interpreter floor. Raising requires-python is a support decision, not a dependency update.
Python dev and build tooling. Covers both layouts in use: [project.optional-dependencies] (unifi-mcp, unraid-mcp) and [dependency-groups] (consistency-check).
Python runtime dependencies. Kept out of the dev group so a shipped bump is never hidden behind a test-only one -- the split unifi-mcp, unraid-mcp, and gandi-mcp already made by hand.
requirements.txt repos (resurgent) have no manifest depTypes to split on, so they group as one.
GitHub Actions. helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests keeps the SHA-pin-with-version-comment shape the workflow convention requires.

Go modules are grouped but not automerged. The one Go repo in the fleet gates on a single `test` check, which is too thin to land a dependency bump unattended. Flip this to true once it also runs vet and a linter.
Terraform and OpenTofu providers are never automerged regardless of update type. A provider bump reaches every repo in the org through the apply pipeline, and the plan output is the review.

Astral tools move fast at 0.x and a minor there can change lint or type behavior. Still automerged -- the failure mode is a red Lint & Format or Type Check on the PR, which blocks the merge rather than landing it.
